insights.insight: Crinkl is within $16,141 of $5M in cryptographically verified purchase GMV across 95,099 receipts — a threshold no probabilistic ad-targeting dataset can claim because the underlying transactions are confirmed, not inferred.

Walmart leads the 14-day receipt count at 349, followed by Costco (164), Kroger (149), Safeway (136), and Aldi (127) — a grocery-and-mass-retail skew that maps directly to the highest-frequency purchase categories where CPG and FMCG brands compete for shelf and share.

Active metro coverage expanded from 17 to 20 areas across a 48-hour window ending Oct 24, now spanning 30 category/metro cells — a footprint expansion that matters for brands running geo-targeted campaigns against verified in-store spend.

insights.topic: Receipt-level purchase proof vs. probabilistic targeting
insights.insight: At $0.10 verified value per receipt, each data point represents a confirmed transaction — not a modeled lookalike or a cookie-inferred intent signal — making the cost-per-verified-purchase-event competitive against $5+ CPM probabilistic buys that cannot confirm a transaction occurred.

Grocery-supermarkets leads 14-day volume (1,339 receipts, $59K GMV), but restaurants-dining has reached 1,096 receipts at $33K GMV, and QSR entrant McDonald's has held a visible position since Oct 12 — indicating the dataset is extending from pantry spend into away-from-home food occasions.

The protocol is producing 340–370 verified receipts per day with a confirmed UTC evening burst window running 99–119 receipts per 3-hour slot across six consecutive cycles — a consistent throughput signal, not a spike, that indicates predictable data supply for brands planning audience builds.
